newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WEU says no word from Tirana on intervention.
newsitem.headline: WEU says no word from Tirana on intervention.

text.p: The Western European Union (WEU), the EU's fledging defence arm, said on Thursday it had not received any request from Albania to provide military assistance to restore order to the troubled Balkan country.

"There has been no formal approach," said one source at the Brussels headquarters of the organisation. He added the mechanism for such an approach did not exist, but President Sali Berisha could ask NATO's European allies individually to intervene.

Reports from the capital Tirana earlier on Thursday said Berisha and all political forces in the country wanted WEU countries to intervene "to restore the constitutional order and to preserve the country's integrity".

WEU diplomats said some of the main European countries, including Italy, France and Britain, believed it was still possible to have a political settlement to the crisis and would be reluctant to become mired in the latest Balkan crisis.
Military analysts said the WEU, which was revamped only a few years ago, did not have the operational capacity at present to conduct a major military intervention.

"Technically, only WEU members can call for a WEU operation. Members who want to be involved could of course call for it to be done under the auspices of the WEU, but at the moment that is most doubtful," said one military source.
